## Summary

DokuReader is an unprivileged, local-first Tkinter desktop application for organizing document references by topic, previewing common file formats, tracking read/unread status, and exporting combined PDFs or a metadata-only JSON library.

## Audience & Personas

- Legal Tech & Compliance Analysts: Professionals managing confidential discovery documents that legally prohibit cloud upload under GDPR/HIPAA.
- Academic Researchers & Literature Curators: Researchers organizing preprints and whitepapers into thematic reading queues without moving originals.
- Offline-First Knowledge Workers & Privacy Advocates: Users demanding zero-egress, transparent local JSON state, and unprivileged execution.
- AI Desktop Application Developers & Coding Agents: Autonomous agents using structured `dokureader-library-v1.json` schemas for downstream document analysis.

## Search Phrases

```text

```

## Disambiguation

DokuReader is not a cloud document manager, hosted OCR platform, general note-taking app, or full citation-management suite. It stores references and read status for local files; LitZentrum covers the broader literature-management workflow in the same doc-bricks family.

## Local Data Boundary & Invariants

- Original documents remain in their existing filesystem locations (INV-INPLACE-03).
- App state is stored locally in `~/.dokubibliothek_state.json` (INV-ISOLATION-05).
- Zero outbound HTTP/S, telemetry, or cloud connections (INV-LOCAL-01).
- Unprivileged user-mode execution under RunAsInvoker principles (INV-RUNAS-02).
- The `dokureader-library-v1.json` export contains topics, paths, file metadata, and read status without embedding private document content.

## Interfaces

- Desktop entrypoint: `python DokuReader.py`
- Windows launcher: `START.bat`
- Windows build launcher: `build_exe.bat`
- Export schema docs: `EXPORTFORMAT.md`
- Store docs: `STORE_LISTING.md`, `PRIVACY_POLICY.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, `store_package.json`
- Version/release readback: `RELEASE_STATUS.md`, `PORTIERUNGSPLAN.md`
- Store readiness gate: `python _WARTUNG/check_store_readiness.py --allow-blockers`
- WACK runner and parser: `python _WARTUNG/run_windows_wack.py --dry-run`

## Test And Validation

- Python tests live under `tests/` (including `test_metadata.py`, `test_release_contract.py`, `test_accessibility_contract.py`, `test_bug_regressions.py`, `test_export_format.py`, `test_store_readiness.py`, `test_windows_wack.py`, `test_store_media.py`, `test_ui_accessibility.py`; 56 collected, 56 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0).
- Web Companion tests live under `web_companion/tests/` (35 Node.js tests verified: 100% green).
- Suites are counted separately, never summed: Python 56 collected / 0 failed (exit 0); Web Companion 35 passed / 0 failed (exit 0); `ruff check .` clean (exit 0); `python tests/source_platform_smoke.py` OK (exit 0). Measured 2026-09-12 with Python 3.12.10 on Windows.
- The former sporadic Tk initialization skip is bounded by at most three setup attempts. Ten independent focused runs produced 60/60 UI test passes without a skip. A real Tk visual smoke captured and reviewed empty, drag-and-drop and text-preview states; receipt: `UI_POLISH_SMOKE.json`.
- MSIX, WACK, signing and Store gates are external and remain unproven by any of these runs.
- Current focused validation: `python -m pytest -ra -v` and `node --test` in `web_companion`.
- Store readiness validation: `python _WARTUNG/check_store_readiness.py --allow-blockers`
- Syntax smoke: `python -m py_compile DokuReader.py manage_translations.py translator.py _WARTUNG/generate_store_media.py _WARTUNG/check_store_readiness.py _WARTUNG/run_windows_wack.py tests/source_platform_smoke.py`
- Workflow YAML should parse before push.

## Version And Release Boundary

- Runtime development version: `DokuReader.py` `APP_VERSION=1.0.1-dev`.
- Python package metadata: `pyproject.toml` `1.0.1.dev0`.
- Windows Store package metadata: `store_package.json` `1.0.1.0`.
- No public release, signed MSIX, WACK certification, or Store submission is verified.
- The metadata-first accessibility contract covers semantic names, roles, states, descriptions, focus order, and read-only preview text. A controlled Tk visual smoke covers empty, drag-and-drop and preview layout states; it does not claim screen-reader, keyboard-hardware, or device acceptance.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit local document libraries, generated releases, converted PDFs, credentials, or `~/.dokubibliothek_state.json`.
- `releases/`, build outputs, local state, SQLite files, tokens, and private/archive folders are ignored.
